unresolved_questions: Will the FDA accept the ASCEND-plus-GEMINI package as sufficient support for an AXS-05 NDA in MDD without further studies?
Will the pending STRIDE-1, ADVANCE-1, AXS-07 and AXS-12 readouts due over the next two quarters replicate GEMINI's pattern or add new risk?
Is the current cash position, plus management's plan not to raise new equity before its Phase 3 readouts, enough to fund operations through the anticipated NDA filing?

own: GEMINI is the second positive well-controlled Phase 3 trial of AXS-05 in MDD, following ASCEND, which the company says is sufficient to support an NDA filing anticipated in the second half of 2020 [c1][c6].
AXS-05 already holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for MDD, granted in March 2019, a status meant to speed agency interaction [c6].

The effect was consistent and rapid: statistically significant improvement over placebo appeared at Week 1 and was significant on every measured secondary endpoint at Week 6, with a tolerability profile that included no reported psychotomimetic effects or weight gain [c3][c4][c5].

Management states it does not anticipate needing new equity financing before its Phase 3 readouts, and four more pivotal or Phase 2 readouts (STRIDE-1, ADVANCE-1, AXS-07 x2, AXS-12) are expected within the next two quarters, giving several near-term catalysts beyond MDD alone [c9][c8].
flat: AXS-05 remains unapproved; no NDA has been filed and no FDA-approved product exists to generate revenue yet [c6].

Cash fell to $43.6 million at September 30, 2019 from $53.8 million three months earlier, and this packet's own scenario calculation implies roughly 4.5 quarters of funding at the recent burn rate -- shorter than management's own 'into Q2 2021' estimate [c9][c11c].
Four additional trial readouts are due within about two quarters, each an independent event with its own binary risk in either direction [c8].
short: The company's own risk disclosure flags that FDA agreement to a mid-trial design change in ADVANCE-1 (dropping the bupropion-monotherapy arm on a data monitoring committee's recommendation) was not yet confirmed as of the filing -- a specific, disclosed source of regulatory uncertainty in one pipeline program [c12].

Net cash used in operating activities over the first nine months of 2019 was about $28.8 million against a cash balance built mainly through financing activities ($58.5 million raised over the same nine months), underscoring dependence on continued capital-markets access for a pre-revenue company [c10].

Management's characterization that the two-trial package 'is sufficient to support submission' of an NDA is the company's own assessment; no public FDA statement committing to accept or approve on that basis is present in this packet [c6].

scene.question: Is a second positive readout enough to buy at today's price, with cash for about four quarters and four more readouts due?

ask_friend.a: GEMINI was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled US trial of 327 adults with moderate to severe depression [c2]. The drug beat placebo on the primary depression score at week six, 16.6 versus 11.9 points, p=0.002, with separation from week one and remission in 39.5% versus 17.3% [c1][c3][c4]. Side effects were dizziness, nausea and headache; one serious event was judged unrelated [c5]. The company says GEMINI plus the earlier ASCEND study supports a filing in the second half of 2020 [c6]; the regulator has not said so.

ask_friend.q: What else is due, and can they pay for it?
ask_friend.a: Four more readouts inside the next two quarters: the same drug in treatment-resistant depression and in Alzheimer's agitation, and a migraine drug in two trials [c7][c8]. Cash was $43.6 million at 30 September, down from $53.8 million three months earlier, with about $10.6 million used in the quarter; at that rate the packet's own scenario gives roughly four and a half quarters [c9][c11b][c11c]. Management says cash lasts into the second quarter of 2021. The company has also proposed a mid-trial design change in the Alzheimer's study that the regulator had not yet agreed [c12].

ask_friend.q: How much is already in the price?
ask_friend.a: The last close is $79.80, a 12-month high, up more than 2,500% over twelve months. Market capitalisation is about $2.75 billion with net cash of about $24 million [c11a]; there is no revenue and no approved product, so revenue multiples do not apply. The price is paying for approval and a launch that have not happened, and for a company that will need to raise money before either.

neutral_title: A small depression-drug developer reports its first pivotal Phase 3 result
player_question: A clinical-stage biotech with one approved franchise attempt (none yet) reports that its lead combination drug hit its primary endpoint in a pivotal MDD trial. Does a single positive pivotal readout in a company with no approved products yet justify taking a position, given remaining regulatory and commercial risk?

inputs.name: net cash (writer tile: Market capitalization and net cash)

caveats: no positive annual revenue in the XBRL facts; revenue multiples not applicable
valuation.note: Derived by the game from eligible inputs; share count and balance-sheet dates differ from the price date. Not a vendor market cap.

claims.text: AXS-05 (dextromethorphan-bupropion) met the primary endpoint in the pivotal Phase 3 GEMINI trial, reducing MADRS depression-severity scores by 16.6 points versus 11.9 points for placebo at Week 6 (p=0.002).

GEMINI was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter U.S. trial of 327 adults with confirmed moderate-to-severe major depressive disorder, randomized 1:1 to AXS-05 (n=163) or placebo (n=164) for 6 weeks.

All secondary endpoints were statistically significant at Week 6, including remission (39.5% vs 17.3%, p<0.001), response (54.0% vs 34.0%, p<0.001), disease severity (p=0.002), functional impairment (p=0.002) and quality of life (p=0.011).
AXS-05 showed statistically significant improvement over placebo as early as Week 1 (MADRS reduction of 7.3 vs 4.9 points, p=0.007), the earliest timepoint assessed.

The most common adverse events were dizziness, nausea, headache, diarrhea, somnolence and dry mouth; one serious adverse event occurred in the AXS-05 arm and was deemed unrelated to study drug; discontinuation due to adverse events was 6.2% (AXS-05) vs 0.6% (placebo); no psychotomimetic effects or weight gain were reported.

the company said GEMINI, together with the previously completed ASCEND trial, is sufficient to support an NDA filing for AXS-05 in MDD, anticipated in the second half of 2020; AXS-05 received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for MDD in March 2019.
AXS-05 is also in the STRIDE-1 Phase 3 trial for treatment-resistant depression and the ADVANCE-1 Phase 2/3 trial for Alzheimer's disease agitation, with Fast Track designations for both indications.

As of the November 7, 2019 update: STRIDE-1 was concluding patient screening with topline results expected Q1 2020; ADVANCE-1 was about 70% enrolled with topline expected in the first half of 2020; the AXS-07 migraine trial MOMENTUM had completed enrollment with topline expected Q4 2019 and a second AXS-07 trial, INTERCEPT, started in October 2019 with topline expected Q1 2020; the AXS-12 narcolepsy trial CONCERT had completed enrollment with topline expected Q4 2019.

the company reported $43.6 million of cash at September 30, 2019, down from $53.8 million at June 30, 2019, and said it believes this cash will fund operations, under its current operating plan, into the second quarter of 2021, with no new equity financing anticipated before its Phase 3 readouts.

Per the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019: cash and cash equivalents were $43,641,861 (vs $13,968,742 at December 31, 2018); total assets $44,439,729 (vs $15,379,279); common stock shares outstanding 34,496,846 (vs 30,087,213); the company stated existing cash should fund operations for at least twelve months from the filing date.
Net cash (cash and cash equivalents less total long-term debt, current and noncurrent) was approximately $23.9 million at September 30, 2019, versus approximately $7.1 million at December 31, 2018.

claims.text: At the trailing nine-month 2019 average quarterly operating cash-outflow rate (about $9.6 million/quarter), the $43.6 million cash balance at September 30, 2019 implies roughly 4.5 quarters (about 13-14 months) of funding on hand from that date -- a simple scenario calculation, not a company forecast.

Per the same December 16, 2019 filing's risk disclosures, the company had proposed to discontinue the bupropion-monotherapy treatment arm of the ADVANCE-1 study on the recommendation of an independent data monitoring committee, with the FDA's agreement to that change not yet confirmed as of the filing.
